subject: Pilot MAP & dataset exchange — FurnishAI evaluation plan
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@furnishai.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ryu <tom.ryu@furnishai.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot MAP & dataset exchange for FurnishAI / Redwood eval

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier — FurnishAI is excited to run a short pilot with Redwood to validate latency/cost and quality on our catalog search prompts. To get this moving we need a mutual action plan (MAP) and a clear path to exchange a small evaluation dataset + prompt pack and test cases. High-level asks from our side: 

- MAP that outlines milestones (kickoff, dataset delivery, acceptance gates, close) and an explicit close-date. We are targeting a pilot kickoff the week of May 3 and acceptance by May 31.
- A downloadable prompt pack / testcase manifest we can run locally and a way for Redwood to run the same tests for side-by-side metrics.
- Usage constraints: data must be used for evaluation only, not retained beyond the agreed period, not used to fine-tune models, and not published.

I've attached our procurement intake form to speed contracting. Can you send a MAP draft and a sample access plan (ephemeral tokens, IP allowlist, SSO, etc.)? Also: does Redwood require an MPA/NDA for exchanging sample content?

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Research Ops, FurnishAI
elena@furnishai.com

Attachments: FurnishAI-procurement-form.pdf (procurement intake form)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@furnishai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & dataset exchange for FurnishAI / Redwood eval

Hi Elena — great to meet you today.

Quick summary and next steps from our side:

1) Attached: MAP-draft-v1.pdf — a lightweight mutual action plan that maps milestones, roles, and deliverables for the pilot. It includes an acceptance gate checklist (pass/fail criteria), and a proposed close timeline that aligns with your May 31 target.
2) Usage constraints we require are listed in section 4 of the MAP: ephemeral access keys, no indexing or storage outside the evaluation environment, and no fine-tuning on supplied samples. We also ask that FurnishAI designate a data steward contact for the dataset.
3) Access model: we typically provide an ephemeral S3 bucket snapshot and short-lived API keys scoped for evaluation; we can also run the tests on our side and share the metrics if you prefer.

If this looks good we can iterate on the MAP and loop in Legal for signatures. I've cc'd Karthik (product) and Monica (solutions engineering) to validate the technical access plan and testcase manifest.

Proposed timeline:
- Apr 23: Review and redlines from FurnishAI legal
- Apr 26: Security checklist items confirmed
- May 3: Pilot kickoff (data exchange + baseline runs)
- May 31: Acceptance decision

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf, testcase-manifest.csv (stub list of sample prompts/testcases)

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0193

Hi Lauren — thanks for the MAP draft. A couple of quick items from our side: 

- FurnishAI legal has one redline on the retention clause: they prefer a 90-day retention window to accommodate internal scheduling (we run a 60–90 day window typically). Can Redwood accommodate 90 days?
- We would like the right to publish an aggregated benchmark case study with Redwood if both sides approve.
- Attached is our completed procurement intake — there are a few standard vendor questions about SOC2, subprocessor list, and data deletion proofs.

If we can get to alignment on retention and the case study clause, Procurement will hand this off to Legal for signature.

Thanks,
Elena

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena@furnishai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-24T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & dataset exchange for FurnishAI / Redwood eval

Elena — appreciate the fast turnaround and the completed intake. Quick responses to the two items: 

- Retention: we can compromise to a 60-day standard but make a one-time exception to 90 days if FurnishAI provides a written schedule for processing and we receive signoff from Security; otherwise default is 60 days. We'll add a clause for an approved case study: aggregated/anonymous metrics only, with prior mutual sign-off on language and figures.

I've attached MAP-draft-v1.1 which includes the conditional retention language and the case study approval step. Monica has expanded the testcase manifest to include the expected file formats and a short checksum process so both sides can validate identical inputs.

Marcus, can you validate the security exception path (we'll need FurnishAI SOC2 evidence or an SSFPO checklist + IP allowlist / SSO setup)? Karthik — can you confirm the acceptance gate criteria in section 3 match our QA runbook?

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.1.pdf, testcase-manifest.csv

Best,
Lauren

Subject: Re: Pilot MAP & dataset exchange for FurnishAI / Redwood eval

Hi Elena / team — Marcus from Security here. Quick checklist and a couple of must-haves to enable the 90-day exception route: 

- SOC2 report or equivalent: FurnishAI must provide the most recent SOC2 Type II report (redacted OK) or an alternative security assessment.
- Access model: SSO (SAML/OIDC) + short-lived, scoped ephem keys for dataset download. No permanent keys.
- IP allowlist for the evaluation endpoints and audit logging enabled for all dataset access.
- No model fine-tuning on supplied evaluation samples — this must be contractually prohibited.
- Data deletion proof: at the end of retention period Redwood will provide a deletion certificate (hashes and deletion job IDs).

I've attached a short security-checklist.xlsx that maps these items to acceptance criteria. If FurnishAI can provide SOC2 and IP allowlist information we can approve the 90-day exception and proceed to signature.

Attachments: security-checklist.xlsx

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com
